title: Microcost Ledger: Token-level cost insights and pricing-control patterns
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Design a console UX for 'Microcost Ledger' — an interactive token-level cost analytics view that lets customers attribute cost to routes, models, operations, and customer cohorts; run ad-hoc exports; and apply pricing/view filters to support billing reconciliation and pricing experiments. Scope includes dashboard-level summaries, a drilldown ledger, export schemas (CSV/Parquet), and a set of pricing UI patterns for toggling displayed charges, rounding/smoothing, and billing snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype for Desktop that demonstrates: summary dashboard, timeline heatmap, per-route/token ledger, and per-model attribution panel.
Export spec included: CSV and Parquet column schema, timezone handling, and row-level attribution keys (request_id, route_id, model_version, token_counts, cost_components).
Pricing UI pattern library documented with interaction states: include/exclude discounts, apply per-token tiering, show hypothetical pricing scenario toggle, and snapshot comparisons.
Handoff artefacts for ENG: component list, accessibility notes, API contract for cost telemetry endpoints, and export job contract.
Stakeholder review approvals from PM, Eng lead, and Revenue ops recorded in ticket comments.
design_notes: Ledger rows represent atomic billing events: aggregated per request with optional expanded token-level rows for long responses.
Primary breakouts: model, route, prompt template, customer segment, and pipeline stage (preprocess/postprocess).
Aggregation windows: support rollups by minute/hour/day with consistent rounding rules to ensure exported sums reconcile with billing system.
Visualization patterns: stacked area for cost over time, heatmap for token density by route, and swipeable per-route detail drawer for mobile fallback.
Performance trade-off: showing full token-level rows for high-volume accounts is expensive — we provide sampled detail with an explict 'full export' action that runs async jobs.
Privacy/security: exports must respect customer data scrubbing preferences and KMS-based encryption for downloads when requested by enterprise customers.

decisions: Adopt a two-tier detail model: sampled inline token-level breakdown + async full export for reconciliation.

Export schema will include canonical attribution keys: timestamp_utc, request_id, route_id, model_version, token_prompt, token_completion, cost_prompt_usd, cost_completion_usd, cost_other_usd, discount_applied, billing_snapshot_id.
Pricing UI patterns: (1) 'Show billed view' vs 'Show raw usage', (2) Scenario toggle to apply hypothetical per-token pricing, (3) Snapshot compare mode for bill disputes.
Rollouts: feature gated behind enterprise flag and gradually enabled to high-usage accounts first.
